newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says troops move farther into rebel land.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says troops move farther into rebel land.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops pushed deeper into northern rebel-held territory on Wednesday, encountering some resistance for the first time in an offensive launched two weeks ago, military officials said.

Troops, backed by artillery, tanks and air cover, advanced 10 km (six miles) into the northern Wanni region, most of which is under the control of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, they said.
"With today's advance, troops have gone about 40 km (25 miles) into rebel territory," one official said.
A Defence Ministry statement said troops captured a bridge after some resistance from rebels holding it. There were no casualties, the ministry said.
The ministry has been tight-lipped on the aim of the latest offensive, which began on February 4 from Vavuniya, a government stronghold 220 km (138 miles) northeast of Colombo.

Military officials said the drive resumed on Monday after troops paused for about 10 days to fortify gains following a 22-km (14-mile) push into rebel territory during the first three days of the offensive, code-named "Edi Bala" (brave force).
On Monday they advanced eight km (five miles).
A military spokesman in Colombo said troops were on the move, but declined to say where they were heading.
But military officials close to the battle area told Reuters troops were closing in on Murunkan, a village about 40 km (25 miles) west of Vavuniya.
Attempts by Reuters to contact LTTE spokesmen in London and Paris for comment were unsuccessful.
The LTTE are fighting a 13-year-old war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
